memory.content: llmHDL/DSLX uses implicit returns, u<N> bit types, explicit width casts, and assert_eq without a Rust-style ! macro.
Avoid reserved keywords such as carry in variable names; use descriptive names.
Annotated return types must match, and mixing bit widths requires explicit type extension; ++ is used for concatenation.
The RISC-V bit-manipulation set discussed includes ror, rol, andn, orn, xnor, pack, packh, brev8, and rev8.
DSLX tests use assert_eq, cover edge cases, and exhaust small input spaces.
DSLX parametric functions use <A: u32, B: u32 = {expr}> syntax and can compute bit widths from parameters.
DSLX arithmetic must account for result width and overflow by explicitly widening operands before operations.
uN denotes an N-bit unsigned value; arrays, tuples, and structs have explicit types, and casts use (value) as type.
RISC-V pack operations combine register halves; pack and packh select lower portions according to the instruction definition.
DSLX type expressions distinguish aliases such as u8 from generic bits[8], so the declared representation and operations must match.

skills.name: dslx-function-write
skills.content: 1. Declare fn name(params) with an explicit return type. 2. Use an implicit final expression as the return. 3. Match every expression to the declared bit width. 4. Add explicit casts for width changes. 5. Compile and test representative inputs.

skills.name: dslx-adder-impl
skills.content: 1. Inspect operand widths. 2. Widen operands with an as cast. 3. Add the widened values. 4. Return a width that accommodates carry. 5. Test all combinations for small inputs.

skills.name: riscv-bitmanip-impl
skills.content: 1. Parse rs1, rs2, and rd. 2. Translate the functional description. 3. Apply the required rotate, logic, or bit-reversal operation. 4. Write the result to rd. 5. Test boundary shift amounts and widths.

skills.name: dslx-type-debug
skills.content: 1. Read the first compiler type error. 2. Compare declared and inferred return types. 3. Check cast compatibility and bit widths. 4. Annotate numeric literals such as u32:42. 5. Recompile with a minimal test.

skills.name: dslx-test-write
skills.content: 1. Add a #[test] function. 2. Use assert_eq(expected, actual). 3. Cover normal, boundary, and overflow cases. 4. Exhaust small input spaces where practical. 5. Keep expected behavior explicit.

skills.name: enum-switch-gen
skills.description: Generate an instruction enum and switch
skills.content: 1. Define an enum for all instruction names. 2. Create a function for each functional description. 3. Switch on the enum and call the matching function. 4. Handle every enum value. 5. Compile and test representative instructions.
